messages:
acme_cust: Hey, we started seeing a bunch of 422 schema errors on streaming tool calls. Looks like the args JSON is getting cut mid-object on about ~2% of requests. Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d. Repro steps in prod: client uses SSE to stream model output which includes a final tool call. Sometimes the client receives truncated args like '{"tool":"charge","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_123","amount":1' and then the stream reconnects. Can you advise?

alex: Thanks for the report — can you paste the raw SSE payload (or a sanitized capture) and the SDK/client you use? Also which edge / region?

acme_cust: sent a sanitized chunk from their proxy log: ```
data: {"type":"tool_call","id":"t-9","payload":{"tool":"charge","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_123","amount":1
``` then new connection opened. They say client uses a Go HTTP client behind a custom edge balancer in eu-west1.

heidi: short follow-up — do you have the full request headers and the X-Request-ID we use on our side? Also, does the SDK send chunked transfer / http2 streaming?

acme_cust: header snippet: ``X-Request-ID: r-0a1b2c3d``, ``Transfer-Encoding: chunked``, ``Content-Type: text/event-stream``. SDK: custom in-house (Go net/http with Flush).

jon: hypothesis — edge balancer appears to be splitting the SSE event mid-JSON and our reassembly logic expects whole SSE "data:" events before parsing. If the proxy emits partial TCP frames that the ingest layer yields as separate SSE events we can end up parsing an incomplete JSON and throwing schema validation.

jon: quick check we did in staging: reproduced by forcing an SSE emitter to emit a JSON right at a 16KB chunk boundary. Our old reassembly would pass the first fragment to the parser and fail.

alex: can you attach the minimal repro script you used? Also, what error code do you return to the client when this happens?

jon: repro (node):
```
const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body: stream });
stream.push('data: {"type":"tool_call","payload":{"tool":"charge","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_123","amount":100}}}

');
// then force split:
stream.push('data: {"type":"tool_call","payload":{"tool":"refund","args":{"invoice_id":"inv_124",');
// small delay then remainder
stream.push('"amount":50}}}

');
```
This reproduces a partial JSON visible to the parser if the ingest layer yields a fragment.

ingest-bot: ingest logs for r-0a1b2c3d show: ``ERROR parser: unexpected end of JSON at byte 124, route=toolcall-handler, code=422`` and a subsequent reconnect event.

heidi: short-term workaround for the customer — they can (a) disable HTTP chunking on their edge so the client sends whole SSE frames, or (b) switch to non-streaming tool call mode for critical flows. Either reduces chance of mid-json handoff.

acme_cust: ok we'll try disabling chunking and test. Do you have a long-term fix plan?

jon: long-term: we should change the ingest parser to buffer across SSE boundaries until we have a syntactically complete JSON (simple brace counting) before attempting schema validation. Need to be careful about memory/doS — cap buffer per-connection and fall back to a safe error after N bytes. Filed INF-3421 to track.

alex: agree. Also want to add more robust logs: when parser fails, include the partial fragment and a char-offset so we can triage quickly.

support-bot: Noted — escalated to eng-runtime, INF-3421 created. ETA: triage tomorrow, small patch planned for canary next week.

heidi: follow-up action items: 1) acme to test disabling chunked on their balancer and report. 2) eng to add buffered reassembly + guardrails. 3) add a customer-facing KB entry describing the streaming chunk/partial-json symptom and mitigations.

acme_cust: disabling chunking reduced errors immediately. Will keep monitoring and share metrics tomorrow. Thanks for the quick help :relieved:

alex: thanks everyone, keeping this thread open until INF-3421 is merged and acme confirms stable. :thumbsup:
